children: Indian benchmark indices are likely to see a negative opening on August 31, tracking GIFT Nifty, which was trading firm at around 24,218.50 in early trade.
Track the latest updates on GIFT Nifty right here on Moneycontrol

In yet another volatile session on August 28, Indian equity indices ended higher, snapping a two-day losing streak, with the Nifty managing to close above 24,150, led by gains in Information Technology stocks.
At close, the Sensex was up 330.92 points or 0.43 percent at 77,264.51, and the Nifty was up 84.80 points or 0.35 percent at 24,175.65.
The broader market underperformed the benchmark indices, with Nifty midcap and smallcap indices ended with little change.
Here is how financial markets across the globe fared overnight:
GIFT Nifty (Down)
GIFT Nifty was trading lower at around 24,218.50 in early trade, indicating a weak opening for the domestic equity markets.
Asian Equities (Down)

Share markets slipped on Monday in Asia as fresh fighting broke out between the United States and Iran, lifting oil prices, while bond yields stayed elevated after investors narrowed the odds on a U.S. rate hike.
US Equities (Down)

Wall ​Street's main indexes ended lower on Friday, with investors turning cautious after Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh reiterated the central bank's focus ‌on fighting inflation, increasing prospects for a rate hike.
The S&P 500 lost 19.23 points, or 0.25%, to 7,711.76 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 138.93 points, ‌or 0.52%, ⁠to 26,402.42.
Dollar Index (Down)

The dollar was quoted in a tight range against Group-of-10 currencies, holding Friday’s gain after hawkish rhetoric from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh lifted expectations of looming interest rate hike. Traders await the G20 finance ministers and central bank governors meeting that begins later Monday.
US Bond Yield (Down)

The yield on 10-year Treasuries was down marginally at 4.71%, while two-year Treasury yields held at 4.33%, after jumping almost 12 basis points on Friday. Yields on 30-year bonds were more contained at 5.2080%, with investors taking some comfort from Warsh's emphasis on fighting inflation.
Asian currencies (Mixed)

Asian currencies were mixed against the US dollar, with the Indonesian Rupiah gaining 0.29% and the Japanese Yen rising 0.09%. The South Korean Won slipped 0.04%, while the Philippines Peso declined 0.10%. The Thai Baht fell 0.19%, and the Taiwan Dollar weakened 0.17%. The China Renminbi eased 0.14%, while the Malaysian Ringgit dropped 0.20%. The Singapore Dollar also edged lower by 0.02%.
Crude (Up)

Oil prices jumped more than $1 a barrel on Monday after the U.S. attacked an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz and drew retaliation from Tehran, as conflict in the Middle East extended into its sixth month.
Gold (Slips)
Gold steadied after falling more than 3% on Friday as US Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh’s pledge to fight inflation lifted bets the US central bank will raise interest rates.
Fund Flow Action

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) sold equities worth over Rs 5000 crore on August 28, however, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) compensated with buying of equities worth Rs 5183 crore, extending buying on the 14th consecutive day.
